subject: question about the "rhyme sequence" example on page 89 of the book

messages.author: 9e5837f0d144e8f1
messages.subject: question about the "rhyme sequence" example on page 89 of the book
parts:
Hello group,

On the P89 of the book there's an example code about adding an "<r>" to every potential rhyme sequence in a sentence. Here's the code:

text <- c("This is a first example sentence.", "And this is a second example sentence.")
gsub("(\\w+?)(\\W+\\w*?)\\1(\\W)", "\\1<r>\\2\\1<r>\\3", text, perl=T)

I can understand this and the code works perfectly, but what about the situation that the rhyme sequence contains more than two words, for example:
text[3] <- "This is a nice example sentence."

Now the result would be "This<r> is<r> a nice<r> example<r> sentence.". Obviously the "example" is consumed in replacing the "nice example" pair, as a result the "example sentence" pair is omitted. However "This<r> is<r> a nice<r> example<r> sentence<r>." is actually my intended result. Any suggestions on the solution?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: question about the "rhyme sequence" example on page 89 of the book
parts:
I've checked some tutorials online about regular expression. I tried to supplement the original code with the following one, for now it seems to work.
text2 <- gsub("(\\w+?)(\\W+\\w*?)\\1(\\W)", "\\1<r>\\2\\1<r>\\3", text, perl=T)
gsub("(\\w+?)(?:<r>)(\\W+\\w*?)\\1(?!<r>)(\\W)", "\\1<r>\\2\\1<r>\\3", text2, perl=T)

Any better idea?

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: question about the "rhyme sequence" example on page 89 of the book
parts:
This is what I can cobble together while at LAX. The loop addresses
(clumsily!) the possibility that there are even more matches/rhymes
than three as in the new example sentence text:

text <- "This sentence is a nice example sentence."
text.new <- gsub("(\\w+?)\\b(.+\\w*)\\1\\b", "\\1<r>\\2\\1<r>", text, perl=TRUE)
for (i in 1:10) {
# both orders of already tagged/untagged matches
text.new <- gsub("((\\w+?)<r>)(.+?)(\\2)(?!<r>)\\b",
"\\1\\3\\4<r>", text.new, perl=TRUE)
text.new <- gsub("(\\w+?)(?!<r>)\\b(.*?)(\\1<r>)", "\\1<r>\\2\\3",
text.new, perl=TRUE)
}
text.new

Cheers,
STG
